detail.body:
The MXFP8 scale swizzle is latency bound. The narrow-K and narrow-M kernels put up to 32 128x4 scale tiles in one 1024-thread CTA, so the scaling factors of a 4096-row activation are swizzled by a single CTA.

Give every 128-row M-tile (row-wise) or 128-column x 32-row block (column-wise) its own CTA, which moves a contiguous chunk with coalesced 16-byte loads and stores through shared memory. Multi-tensor launches group tiles per CTA only when the grid would otherwise be very large. The existing kernels remain for NVFP4, unaligned buffers, and row-wise scales too wide for 48 KB of shared memory.

files.patch:
@@ -342,6 +342,12 @@ Kernel Configuration
    :Default: ``0``
    :Description: Disable NVRTC (CUDA Runtime Compilation) support. When set to ``1``, runtime kernel compilation is disabled. Existing transpose operations select their static fallback automatically. NVFP4 4over6 quantization, fused softmax, and normalization paths require their corresponding ``NVTE_BUILD_LEGACY_STATIC_NVFP4``, ``NVTE_BUILD_LEGACY_STATIC_FUSED_SOFTMAX``, or ``NVTE_BUILD_LEGACY_STATIC_NORM`` CMake option to have been enabled when the library was built; otherwise no static fallback is available.
 
+.. envvar:: NVTE_MXFP8_PER_TILE_SWIZZLE
+
+   :Type: ``int`` (0 or 1)
+   :Default: ``0``
+   :Description: Swizzle MXFP8 scaling factors for GEMM with kernels that give each 128-row tile of scaling factors (row-wise) or each 128-column by 32-row block (column-wise) its own thread block, instead of batching 32 tiles in one block. This lowers the latency of swizzling the scaling factors of tensors with few tiles, such as activations.
+
 .. envvar:: NVTE_USE_CUTLASS_GROUPED_GEMM
 
    :Type: ``int`` (0 or 1)

inline_comments.body: **Larger chunks lack useful coverage** This case selects `tile_swizzle_col_multi_kernel<128>`, but its scale buffer has only four rows: `M / MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE = 128 / 32`. It never checks scale rows beyond the first 32, so mistakes in the larger-chunk path can pass these tests. Add a case such as `{20, 4224, 2048, false}` to check a full 128-row chunk and a clipped final chunk against the reference. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

issue_comments.body:
Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Medium impact]** The PR appears safe to merge; no blocking issue was found.

Summary

Adds optional MXFP8 scale-swizzle kernels that give small tiles separate thread blocks to reduce latency. - `NVTE_MXFP8_PER_TILE_SWIZZLE` defaults to off. - Large grids group tiles, while unsupported inputs keep the existing kernels. - Tests cover both flag settings, multiple launches, grouped tiles, and clipped chunks. - The earlier unnumbered coverage comment is addressed by `{20, 4224, 2048, false}`, which checks a full 128-row chunk and a final four-row chunk. - No new actionable issues were found. CUDA tests were not run.

issue_comments.body: LGTM. Perf is definitely better compared to the existing kernels for DSV3 sizes of weights/activations. However, currently the kernels are gated by env variable, since we want to make sure the perf is consistent across the board for all sizes. The variable will be removed once that is verified.
